code.originalText: Day 12: end of metronidazole and start of paromomycin, blood count, CRP and liver tests, mood and safety review

text.paragraph: Day 12: end of metronidazole and start of paromomycin, blood count, CRP and liver tests, mood and safety review. [S]

Mr. Ramanujan returns at the end of ten days of metronidazole. At the nurse's call on the third day his fever had already broken, and he has had none since. The ache under his right ribs is much less and no longer catches his breath. Metronidazole gave him a metallic taste and some nausea, eased by taking it with food; he finished every dose three days ago and started paromomycin the next day, which has loosened his stools to twice a day. He asked about the capsule shells, which contain gelatin, and after discussion decided to take them as prescribed. He has no numbness or tingling. He met the dietitian and is cooking once a day for two meals. He has seen the counselor twice. He is sleeping better and has returned to his work for a few hours a day. [S]

Amebic liver abscess: a single 6.2 x 5.4 cm abscess in the right lobe (segment VII) on ultrasound, Entamoeba histolytica antibody positive, blood cultures negative, years after two episodes of dysentery in India; treated with metronidazole and then paromomycin; synthetic modern diagnosis linked to the hepatic amoebiasis later proposed for his illness

Amebic liver abscess (A06.4). Good response: afebrile from day 3, pain much less. White cells 8.9, CRP 24 mg/L from 92; alkaline phosphatase 168 U/L from 214; ALT 34 U/L; albumin 3.5 g/dL. No imaging is needed while he improves. [S]
Finish paromomycin, two capsules three times a day, four more days.
Loose stools are expected; drink well.

Vitamin B12 deficiency with anemia (D51.3). Hemoglobin 11.6 g/dL from 11.2 and rising; platelets 380. A reticulocyte count one week after starting replacement was not ordered. [S]
Continue B12 1,000 micrograms daily.
Blood count at six weeks.

Adjustment disorder with depressed mood (F43.21). PHQ-9 10 and GAD-7 7, from 12 and 9. Safety reviewed: no thoughts of suicide or self-harm; safety plan current. [S]
Continue counseling weekly.
Call home on a fixed day each week, as he planned.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: Official American Thoracic Society/Infectious Diseases Society of America/Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Clinical Practice Guidelines: Diagnosis of Tuberculosis in Adults and Children (2017); DPDx: Amebiasis (laboratory diagnosis, including antibody detection in extraintestinal disease) (2026); A Review of the Global Burden, New Diagnostics, and Current Therapeutics for Amebiasis (2018); Position of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics: Vegetarian Diets (2016); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, anemia and depression monographs (2026); Depression and Suicide Risk in Adults: Screening (2023); VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for Assessment and Management of Patients at Risk for Suicide (2024)

Follow-up: Review at six weeks with the final sputum cultures, blood count, liver tests, vitamin B12 and mood. Call for fever, return of the right-sided pain, or diarrhea that does not settle after paromomycin. Next scheduled visit 1917-02-23: six weeks: recovery, final sputum cultures, liver tests before rifampin, vitamin B12, mood, influenza vaccine. [S]
